requirement:
A delivered read page records the dependencies retained by that page under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. Each continuation of a
node or mapped source read retains the original node identity and content
fingerprint; reading a later page does not observe a newer version. A change
to that node's fingerprint can invalidate the evidence even if it happens
between pages. Agent tools record on delivery. Discovery pages record no evidence
inputs, just like their initial result. Preparing an undelivered page records
no read.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.pages.inputs`. Every clause describes behavior that can be observed. The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface.

- "A delivered read page records the dependencies retained by that page": this constrains what evidence is recorded. It does not say how the recording is built. Evidence recorded from a different place in the code would behave the same.
- "Each continuation ... retains the original node identity and content fingerprint; reading a later page does not observe a newer version": a design that re-read and re-fingerprinted the node on each page would break this clause by observable behavior, because it would see a newer version. A snapshot, a cached page set or a stored fingerprint would all satisfy it equally. The retention mechanism is therefore discretionary.
- "Agent tools record on delivery. Discovery pages record no evidence inputs. Preparing an undelivered page records no read.": these are outcome rules about when evidence is or is not recorded.

The cited `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs` supplies context only. It covers observation contents and de-duplication, and also describes behavior. The review roots are empty, so there are no implementation roots to map, and none are needed. Tests supply the evidence for this requirement's behavioral obligations.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each observable obligation of `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.pages.inputs`. I did not request implementation source.

- **Delivered read pages record their retained dependencies.** In `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[outline_continuations_keep_the_file_and_complete_ordered_items]`, each page of a paged `read_node` on a file root asserts `dependencies == [Dependency::Node(code.rs#, fingerprint of root_text)]`. In `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[graph_tools_record_delivered_snapshots_and_prepared_pages_do_not_record_delivery]`, the agent runs `read_node` and then `get_next_page` on an 18,000-character node. It asserts that the recorded `Dependency::Node` carries the full contents as its fingerprint.

- **Continuations keep the original identity and fingerprint, and a later page does not see newer content.**
  - The root-read test changes the domain text after the first read, once the first page is already prepared. Every continuation page still reports the original fingerprint, and the concatenated page text equals the original text.
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[graph_read_pages_retain_the_prepared_snapshot_after_contents_change]` changes the graph contents between pages through `ChangingProvider`. It asserts that the graph was read only once (`reads == [1]`) and that the single recorded dependency has the original fingerprint. It also asserts that the concatenated page text equals the original. A change between pages therefore cannot alter the recorded fingerprint.

- **Agent tools record on delivery.** The first test checks that the prepared and delivered input counts differ. Prepared is 3 and delivered is 3 after the successful run. After the two failed runs, prepared is 6 and delivered is 4.

- **Discovery pages record no evidence inputs.**
  - The outline test asserts `delivery.dependencies.is_empty()` for the initial `outline_source` result and for every `get_next_page` continuation.
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[listing_continuations_return_complete_paths_from_the_original_listing]` asserts empty dependencies for the initial `list_sources` result and for every continuation.

- **Preparing an undelivered page records no read.** In the first agent test, a `read_node` is prepared but the agent then fails, so it is never delivered. The test asserts `ctx.dependencies().is_empty()`. A contrasting case, where `contents_of_current_node` is used, shows that dependencies are recorded when the read is actually requested. The retention test's single-read assertion also shows that preparing continuation pages causes no extra reads.

The invalidation clause only says a changed fingerprint can invalidate the evidence. It follows from the recorded fingerprint being the original, which these tests assert. The invalidation check itself is not part of this requirement's own obligations. No gap or ambiguity needs a correction.

Finishing a verification includes every successful tracked node read in its
`Fingerprinted`, whether ordinary code or a model tool requested it. Each observation
contains the node identity and the fingerprint of the contents actually supplied.
A failed read returns an error without inventing a successful observation.
Repeating an identical observation adds no information. Reading the same
identity with two different fingerprints preserves both observations.
